documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 05/09/2025, 17:40.

CC: L ear pain x3 days.

HPI: 25F with type 1 diabetes on insulin, well controlled, followed by endocrinology (last seen about 8 months ago). Three days of left ear pain, much worse when she tugs on the ear lobe. Ear feels plugged and she hears less on that side. No discharge from the ear. No fever, chills, headache, dizziness or facial weakness. Went swimming in a lake about 5 days ago.

PMH: T1DM. PSH: third molar extraction at 18.
Meds: insulin glargine 20 units SC qhs; insulin aspart 8 units SC before meals; glucagon 1 mg IM PRN.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: maternal aunt Hashimoto; paternal grandfather T2DM.
SH: graduate student. Never smoker. Alcohol rare.

Exam: vitals reviewed, afebrile. Uncomfortable but nontoxic. L external auditory canal erythematous and swollen nearly shut, marked tenderness over the tragus; TM cannot be seen past the swelling. No discharge. No periauricular swelling or mastoid tenderness. Facial nerve intact. R ear normal. No cervical adenopathy.

Data: fingerstick glucose 180 mg/dL.

MDM: painful otitis externa of the left ear in an insulin-dependent diabetic after freshwater exposure. Given diabetes, treated as malignant otitis externa with antipseudomonal coverage and prompt ENT evaluation.

Dx: Malignant otitis externa, left ear.

Rx: ciprofloxacin 750 mg PO BID; ofloxacin otic 0.3% 10 drops L ear BID x14 days. Keep the ear dry, no swimming. Monitor glucose more often while ill.

Disposition: discharged home in stable condition. Follow up with ENT within days, call PCP Monday. Return for fever, spreading swelling, facial weakness, severe headache or worsening pain.

documents.title: Went to the ER last night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I went to the ER last night for my left ear. It's been hurting since Tuesday and I can barely hear out of it. They said it's an outer ear infection and because I have diabetes they called it malignant otitis externa?? They gave me cipro pills and ear drops and said I need to see ENT soon. I don't have an ENT. Sugars have been running a little higher than usual. Pain is about the same this morning.

documents.title: RE: Went to the ER last night
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know. Keep taking both, keep the ear dry, and keep a closer eye on your sugars; infections and cipro can both push them around. I'll do a video visit with you Monday morning and get ENT lined up. If you get a fever, swelling around the ear, a headache that won't quit or any weakness in your face, go back to the ER.

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, pt at home in Easthampton, identity confirmed.

Seen in a regional ED Friday evening for 3 days of left ear pain after lake swimming 5 days before that. Per her and her discharge paperwork: canal swollen shut, tragal tenderness, TM not visible, fingerstick 180. Diagnosed with malignant otitis externa given her T1DM; started ciprofloxacin 750 mg BID and ofloxacin otic drops. ED record not yet received.

Today: day 3 of treatment. Pain about the same, maybe slightly less at night. Ear still plugged, hearing muffled on the left. No drainage, no fever, no headache, no facial droop. Glucose running higher than her usual; no lows. Taking cipro with food, drops twice a day.

Observed on video: comfortable, no visible swelling behind or in front of the ear, face symmetric.

A/P
1. Malignant otitis externa, left, on ciprofloxacin and ofloxacin drops from the ED. Needs ENT this week given diabetes. Urgent ENT referral placed and called through.
2. T1DM: expect some rise in sugars with infection; correction per her endo plan, call endo if readings stay high or she has ketones. Cipro can also cause lows, keep checking.
3. Cipro and tendons: hold the long runs until the course is done, stop and call for any heel or calf pain.
Return precautions reviewed.

documents.body: Urgent ENT referral faxed with today's note and the fill history. ENT office able to see her Wed 5/14 at 1:30. Pt notified by phone, will bring her ED discharge papers.

reports.text:
Technique: axial thin-section images through both temporal bones without intravenous contrast, with coronal reformats.
Comparison: none.
Findings: Soft-tissue thickening of the left external auditory canal with narrowing of the canal lumen. The bony canal walls are intact with no erosion. The left middle ear cavity and ossicles are normal. Left mastoid air cells are well aerated and clear. No soft-tissue collection in the periauricular region. Skull base and temporomandibular joint normal. The right temporal bone is normal.
reports.conclusion: Soft-tissue thickening and narrowing of the left external auditory canal without bony erosion. Middle ear and mastoid clear.

documents.title: Otolaryngology Consultation
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside otolaryngology group
Date of consultation: 05/14/2025
Referring: primary care

Thank you for asking us to see Abigail Lemieux, a 25-year-old graduate student with type 1 diabetes, for left ear pain treated in an ED on 5/9 as malignant otitis externa.

She developed left otalgia after swimming in a lake, with fullness and reduced hearing. On ciprofloxacin 750 mg twice daily and ofloxacin otic drops since 5/9; pain now slowly easing. No otorrhea, fever, vertigo or facial weakness.

Meds: glargine 20 units qhs, aspart 8 units before meals, glucagon kit, ciprofloxacin, ofloxacin otic.
Allergies: none known.

Exam: left canal edematous and erythematous; tragal tenderness and pain with traction on the pinna. Under the microscope the canal was debrided and a sample sent for culture; no granulation tissue at the bony-cartilaginous junction. After cleaning the TM could be glimpsed only partly. A wick was placed. Right ear normal. Facial nerve function intact and symmetric. No cervical lymphadenopathy.

CT temporal bones today: soft-tissue thickening of the left canal without bony erosion; middle ear and mastoid clear.
ESR 41.
Culture (final 5/17): Pseudomonas aeruginosa, ciprofloxacin sensitive.

Impression: early necrotizing (malignant) otitis externa, left, in a patient with type 1 diabetes. Imaging shows no bone involvement.

Plan:
- Continue ciprofloxacin 750 mg twice daily for a total of six weeks from the start on 5/9.
- Ofloxacin drops to finish 14 days; wick to come out on its own or at a nurse check.
- Strict water precautions.
- Good glucose control with her endocrinologist.
- Return in about five weeks with a repeat ESR; sooner for worsening pain, drainage, headache or facial weakness.

Sincerely,
Otolaryngology

documents.title: Otolaryngology Follow-up
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside otolaryngology group
Date of visit: 06/20/2025

Ms. Lemieux returns six weeks into treatment for left necrotizing otitis externa. Pain resolved within the first two weeks. Hearing back to normal by her report. Finished the drops in May; wick fell out on its own. Tolerated ciprofloxacin without tendon pain. Sugars back to her usual.

Exam: left canal healed, skin normal, no debris, no granulation. TM intact, mobile, normal landmarks. Right ear normal. Facial nerve intact.

ESR today 12, down from 41.

Impression: left necrotizing otitis externa, resolved after six weeks of oral ciprofloxacin.

Plan: stop ciprofloxacin today. Keep the ear dry while swimming for the rest of the summer (ear plugs). Return as needed; she knows to come back promptly for any recurrence of ear pain given her diabetes.

Otolaryngology

documents.title: Ear update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw ENT on Friday. They said the ear is healed and the blood test came down, so I'm done with the cipro! Hearing is normal again. Can I start doing long runs again?

documents.title: RE: Ear update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news. Yes, ease back into the long runs over a couple of weeks now that the cipro is done, and stop if you get any Achilles or calf pain. Earplugs if you swim. We haven't received the ENT note yet; I'll keep an eye out for it.

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly physical.

Interval: left necrotizing (malignant) otitis externa in May after lake swimming. ED 5/9, ENT 5/14 (CT without bone involvement, ESR 41, Pseudomonas on culture), six weeks of ciprofloxacin; ENT follow-up 6/20 healed, ESR 12, cipro stopped. ENT follow-up letter arrived in August. No ear symptoms since. Uses earplugs swimming. Resolving on the problem list today.

Diabetes: still with the outside endocrinology group, seen in the spring per her, no changes; no letter from them since last fall's. Glargine 20 qhs, aspart 8 before meals, glucagon kit current. No lows. Optometry in July: no retinopathy.

Back to running long distances without problems.
NKDA. Never smoker. Alcohol rare.

ROS negative. PHQ-9: 1.

Exam: vitals as charted. Ears: both canals clean, TMs intact and normal. Rest of HEENT normal. Neck and thyroid normal. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. Feet: no lesions, pulses intact, monofilament normal. Neuro normal.

A/P
1. Malignant otitis externa, left: resolved.
2. T1DM: controlled per endo. Yearly CMP, lipids, TSH, urine microalbumin, CBC today.
3. Prevention: Pap normal 2024, next 2027. Flu and COVID in October when the clinic gets supply.
4. Physical next fall.

documents.title: Lab results

documents.body: All of Tuesday's labs are normal, including blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol, thyroid and the urine protein screen. Nothing to change. We'll text when flu and COVID shots are in.
